Authority: independently opened the actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx with openpyxl: Quality Checks!A42:D42 says "Pass/fail behaviors are binary; craft and degree-of-quality are likert with described anchors." Read Internal Quality Checks row 42 as interpretation only; SKILL.md, Known false positives explicitly resolves its binary/weighted note in favor of shipped Likert. references/quality-checks.md:168-170 requires anchors at each level; staged-task-contract.md:96,132-140 allows five-point Likert in scored dimensions and requires binary gates. The deterministic workbook check-rubric-schema.py row 29 and deterministic-checks.md recipe agree. Current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md, Independent credit and Runtime and model evidence, govern outcome independence and runtime limits.

Complete criterion inspection and a fresh read-only tomllib/anchor assertion found 73 criteria: 2 binary gates, 58 binary Functional, 7 binary Polish and 6 Visual Likert. Both gate judge.toml files:20 use binary for actual authored execution or clean-context saved-record retrieval (render:23-27; constraints:23-29), not a subjective craft threshold. All Functional descriptions (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:24-428) express observable execution, timing, source display, console, saving, conflict or theme-switch outcomes. The potentially visual editor checks are explicit public feature-presence requirements (environment/instructions/ui.md:5; functional/judge.toml:312-330). S19 in functional/prompt.md:342-348 requires actual monospacing, line numbers and token colouring while freeing palette/package; S34:395 expressly assigns contrast, palette and aesthetic readability to Visual.

All seven Polish descriptions were reviewed (tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:17-78). Mobile pane/control access, accessible names, actual keyboard reachability, visible focus and the keyboard library route are binary operability requirements. interaction_feedback:68 asks for an observed acknowledgement of one ordinary supported action (e.g. new output or a clear empty-console state), not exceptional quality. workspace_organisation:77 asks whether the specific surfaces and current filename/library can be identified, expressly accepting labels OR layout and prescribing no arrangement. These are minimum recognisability checks, not a binary aesthetic-quality score. Polish prompt:24-39 and 43-49 preserves independent results and permits native/composite controls.

Every Visual criterion is type="likert", points=5, with a substantive anchor for each integer 1-5: visual_typography (visual/judge.toml:18-29), visual_color_and_contrast (:33-44), visual_spacing_and_layout (:48-59), visual_hierarchy_and_scanability (:63-74), visual_overall_craft (:78-89), visual_responsive_consistency (:93-104). Anchors distinguish minor distractions, repeated inconsistency and severe impairment; full credit accepts native components, simple layouts and harmless imperfections (:25,40,55,70,85,100). visual/prompt.md:39-43 specifies integer raw 1-5 and (raw-1)/4 normalization, explicitly rejecting perfection or preferred-style requirements. :17-22 separates binary mobile operability and actual theme switching from visual composition and resulting presentation.

Adversarial source review: a conforming plain native-control layout with labelled or recognisable panes, a tabbed narrow-screen workspace, native focus rings and simple coherent typography can pass the binary usability thresholds and receive Visual 5; the explicit allowances defeat a false failure for lack of decorative craft. Conversely, attractive chrome with an unreachable library control or no visible Run/Clear acknowledgement fails the corresponding binary outcome even if its visual anchors are high. An otherwise functional interface with several cramped text treatments can keep binary functionality while receiving visual_typography 3 (:27); binary craft would lose this distinction, but these criteria preserve it. These are textual counterfactuals, not executed alternative-app runs; no credible type/anchor false-pass or false-fail was established.

Raw evidence calibration: RESULTS.json facts.S19.editor_monospace.evidence.font.value records monospace family with equal narrow/wide width 52; facts.S19.editor_syntax_colouring.evidence.languages records distinct token colours in each of JS/HTML/CSS; facts.S16.console_clear_control.evidence shows populated logs becoming "Console is clear. Logs and errors appear here." These observations support the feature-presence interpretation, not aesthetic grading. Fresh SHA256 comparisons matched the frozen Functional judge and prompt against RESULTS.json functional_sha256 and prompt_sha256. The log explicitly describes "Continuous local reference browser proof; no LLM/provider/platform execution" and oracle_score_claimed=false. No configured judge Likert assignments, full judge duration, hosted QC, Oracle grade or target-model score are established. Those separate runtime measurements are not prerequisites for this source-level type/anchor conclusion; run_verdict is PARTIAL accordingly.
